categories.title: Getting started
categories.intro: One or two places, one service each: the processes the tutorials build, step by step.

categories.title: Petri net patterns
categories.intro: Forks, joins and loops: classic nets, each place a host of its own and every transition rules installed on it.

categories.title: Claims and inventory
categories.intro: Real services deciding the route. Claims triage pays a claim of up to 2,500 at once and sends a larger one to Assess, a Node.js service on the internet that accepts claims up to 4,000 and rejects the rest. The inventory service keeps its own stock on its host and reserves one unit per order; when it runs out, the supplier on another host delivers more after a lead time, and the delivered stock travels back inside the order, because hosts share no memory.

categories.title: Credit and lending
categories.intro: Real services making lending decisions. Validation checks that each application has an identifier, an income and an amount. The credit check grades the credit score (700 and over strong, 620 to 699 review, below that weak) and records an enquiry against the application; the fraud check reports the application's fraud risk, and the fraud bureau cannot be reached for one application in five. Underwriting joins the two: high fraud risk or a score under 600 is declined, 700 and over with low risk is approved, the rest is conditional. With no fraud result the loan is abandoned, and a Signal node launches a compensation process that withdraws the credit enquiry. The applications are synthetic; every decision is the services' own.

categories.title: Healthcare
categories.intro: Real services, not stubs: each department is a Java service applying clinical rules to every patient. Triage sets a priority from the presenting condition, heart rate, oxygen saturation and pain score, and sends a confirmed heart attack or stroke straight to treatment. The laboratory checks troponin, BNP, creatinine and electrolytes against reference ranges and critical limits; cardiology reads the ECG and grades the cardiac risk; diagnosis combines the three results into a diagnosis and a disposition, from ICU admission to outpatient follow-up; treatment records the medications given in its own database. The patients are synthetic, a fixed mix of emergency cases from chest pain to heart attack and stroke; every decision is made by the services as the run goes.

examples.title: The P2 tutorial
examples.description: A stochastic service on node P2: true ends the token, false sends it back to try again.

examples.title: Two places in a row
examples.description: P1 passes each token on to P2; each place decides true or false.

examples.title: A credit check
examples.description: The service tutorial's process: a credit limit service approves an application of up to 5,000 and refers the rest.

examples.title: Fork and join
examples.description: P1 forks to P2 and P3, on separate hosts; both must arrive before P4 runs.

examples.title: Double join
examples.description: Three branches, two joins: P4 waits for P2 and P3, then P6 waits for P4 and P5.

examples.title: Rendezvous
examples.description: Two tokens, one in each place, meet at a join and go round again.

examples.title: Extra fork child
examples.description: A place forks more branches than it holds token numbers for, and the hosts still tell the branches apart.

examples.title: Traffic lights
examples.description: An intersection: north-south and east-west lights hand over through forks, joins and feedback. An open process: the lights never stop, so the replay ends where the records were collected.

examples.title: Dining philosophers
examples.description: Five philosophers on five hosts share five forks; each eats only when its join holds both.

examples.title: Dining philosophers, deadlocked
examples.description: Every philosopher starts holding one fork: each join waits for a fork that never comes.

examples.title: Insurance claims
examples.description: Triage pays a claim of up to 2,500 at once; a larger one goes to Assess, a service on the internet that accepts up to 4,000.

examples.title: Inventory and supplier
examples.description: The inventory starts with five units on its host; when they run out, the supplier delivers three more after a lead time, once, and later orders are cancelled.

examples.title: Validation on its own
examples.description: The first step of the loan process, on one host: validate each application.

examples.title: Credit check over REST
examples.description: The same credit check, its rule (approve up to 5,000) answered by a Node.js service over the internet instead of on the host.

examples.title: Fraud screen, then credit
examples.description: A fraud screen, then the credit check over REST. The fraud screen still runs the starting code the editor wrote for it, which takes clear and review in turn until the real rule is written.

examples.title: Loan application, with compensation
examples.description: Credit and fraud checks join at underwriting; an abandoned loan signals a second process to withdraw its credit enquiry.

examples.title: Two processes, shared services
examples.description: The loan process (v001) and a pre-screen (v002) run at once on the same validation and credit hosts.

examples.title: Priority: an urgent burst
examples.description: Forty background pre-screens (v002) are under way when fifteen urgent loans (v001) arrive and go first.

examples.title: Emergency department
examples.description: Triage sends a confirmed heart attack or stroke straight to treatment; other patients are worked up by laboratory, cardiology and radiology, whose results join at diagnosis.

examples.title: Federated radiology
examples.description: Imaging requests from another hospital: this hospital's radiology service chooses the imaging protocol for each and returns its findings, marked for the hospital that asked.

examples.title: Three versions at once
examples.description: The emergency department, a triage canary and federated radiology requests, run together on six hosts: the same clinical services serve all three.
